TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Karachi approaches
DATE 24 October 2028 · 0630 local
SIDE Pakistan Navy
WINDOW 110 min, closes at 165
Z-9 family; the Navy flies the Z-9EC, the Pakistani Pack's Z-9CE (family reference: a PLAN airframe). Photo: Sparktour · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"Readiness is critical to an effective deterrence, not only in Air Force, but across all domains."
- Air Vice-Marshal Harvey Reynolds, Deputy Chief of Air Force, RAAF

KARACHI APPROACHES, 0630. MT SINDH VOYAGER and MT ORMARA TRADER weighed at first light from the outer roads with crude for the refinery and diesel for the city. They are the first tankers to sail for Karachi since the war-risk listing, and the masters sailed on the Navy's word that they would be escorted.

Two Meridian armed trawlers left the coast west of Sonmiani before dawn and are running east at their best speed. Meridian calls them escorts. Last week one of them ordered a Liberian tanker to divert to a Meridian terminal and put a burst of 40 mm across her bow when she would not. A third trawler, with no nets out, has kept station on the convoy since it weighed.

Bring both tankers within six miles of the Karachi pilot station, twenty-six miles north-east. The convoy's task is complete when both are inside that circle. Your ships are weapons Free. If the Meridian boats close the convoy, stop them. The trawler keeping company is Meridian's eyes on the convoy; she has not fired.
Fishing dhows, an outbound freighter and the morning Dubai service are on the water and in the air. Identify before you fire.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Commander Pakistan Fleet, Karachi
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Karachi runs on what these two ships carry. Bring both to the pilot station. Meridian's boats are armed and will order the masters to divert; if they close the convoy, stop them. Every dhow on this water is a fishing boat until you have identified it as something else.
• Bring both tankers within six miles of the Karachi pilot station
• Lose neither tanker
• Sink the two Meridian boats if they close the convoy
• Harm no dhow, freighter or airliner

Your task group, with its helicopter if one is embarked. Convoy: MT Sindh Voyager and MT Ormara Trader. Opposing: two Meridian armed trawlers, and a third keeping company. Neutral: fishing dhows, a freighter and an airliner. PAF Base Masroor is open to your helicopters.

The planned window is 110 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 55 minutes more; the operation is closed at 165 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
